channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Andijan establishes $28 million leather and footwear industrial zone with 17 projects
item.description: A new leather and footwear industrial zone worth $28 million has been established in Andijan, Uzbekistan. The zone will host 17 projects and has already created 2,500 new jobs.

item.title: Tashkent hosts international conference on modern engineering education approaches
item.description: An international conference on modern engineering education was held at the Tashkent Institute of Textile and Light Industry. The event focused on preparing qualified personnel for modern mechanical engineering and digitalization.

item.title: Andijan textile factory integrates AI and dual education for eco-friendly production
item.description: An Andijan textile enterprise, "Eco Cotton," is implementing artificial intelligence and dual education systems. The project, supported by President Mirziyoyev, focuses on producing eco-friendly textiles from local raw materials for domestic and international markets. The factory invested $10 million, creating 1,000 jobs and aiming for 25 billion soms in annual state budget revenue.

item.title: Andijan launches $25 million 'smart' water meter factory with 80% automation
item.description: A new factory producing "smart" water meters worth $25 million has been launched in Andijan. The production process is 80% automated, with plans to reach 70% localization by 2030. The facility aims to meet future demands for advanced water management technology.

item.title: Bishkek police seize over 6,000 doses of synthetic drugs
item.description: Bishkek police have arrested two individuals suspected of distributing synthetic drugs via hidden caches. Authorities seized approximately 1 kilogram of Alpha-PVP, valued at over 4 million soms, which could constitute more than 6,000 doses. Investigations are ongoing to identify other potential accomplices.

item.title: Russian education remains in demand in Central Asia, says Rossotrudnichestvo representative
item.description: Russian education is highly sought after in Central Asia due to historical and cultural ties, according to Irina Staroselskaya, head of Rossotrudnichestvo in Uzbekistan. Uzbekistan has requested 810 state-funded places for the 2026/27 academic year, with universities noting the diligence of Uzbek students.

item.title: Uzbek President Proposes Incentives for Businesses Creating Jobs for Low-Income Citizens
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev suggested attracting entrepreneurs to employ low-income citizens by offering preferential loan and tax terms for businesses creating jobs. He emphasized the need for targeted aid, ensuring support reaches those genuinely in need. Local authorities have been granted necessary powers to work with low-income families and ensure employment.

item.title: Tajikistan and China to Expand Cooperation in Training Civil Servants
item.description: Tajikistan's Academy of Public Administration and China's Lanzhou University of Technology signed a Memorandum of Understanding to enhance cooperation in education, research, and academic exchange. The agreement includes plans for faculty and student exchanges, joint research on Central Asian issues, and training programs for Tajik civil servants.

item.title: Second International Textile Forum Opens in Dushanbe
item.description: The Second International Textile Forum "Tajikistan-2026" opened in Dushanbe on September 23, 2026. Organized by the Ministry of Industry and New Technologies, the event brought together representatives from 15 countries to discuss the textile industry's development, foreign investment, and international experience exchange.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Direct Bishkek-Sanya Flight Route to China
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has proposed to China the opening of a direct flight route between Bishkek and the resort city of Sanya. Discussions also covered a China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway and infrastructure projects.

item.title: Uzbekistan to resume hosting international ATP and WTA tennis tournaments
item.description: Uzbekistan will resume hosting international tennis tournaments under the auspices of ATP, WTA, and ITF starting October 1, 2026. A presidential decree aims to popularize tennis, develop talented athletes, improve sports infrastructure, and enhance performance in prestigious competitions. Tournament costs will be covered by sponsorships.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and China discuss oil refinery and pipeline construction
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers, Erlist Akunbekov, met with executives from Chinese oil and gas corporations CNPC and Sinopec in Beijing. The discussions focused on the potential construction of an oil refinery and a related pipeline.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Academy of Law Enforcement granted CIS base status for anti-corruption
item.description: The Academy of Law Enforcement of Uzbekistan has been granted status as a base educational organization of the CIS for combating corruption. This decision was made at the 11th meeting of the Interstate Council for Combating Corruption in Minsk, where member states' representatives participated.

item.title: New School Building Inaugurated in Kurush Village, Spitamen District
item.description: A new school building was commissioned in Kurush village, Spitamen district, on September 22, 2026. The facility, funded by parents, sponsors, and local authorities, accommodates 320 students and features modern classrooms.

item.title: Tajikistan and Belarus Free Economic Zones Discuss Expanding Trade and Investment
item.description: Leaders of Tajikistan's Dangara SEZ and Belarus's Gomel-Raton SEZ held an online meeting to discuss expanding trade and investment cooperation, developing logistics, and exchanging experience. Both sides emphasized strengthening bilateral economic ties and creating favorable investment conditions.

item.title: Uzbekistan Transforms Aral Sea Region Towards Sustainable Development and New Economy
item.description: Uzbekistan is actively transforming the Aral Sea region, moving beyond ecological disaster recovery to foster a new economy. Initiatives include large-scale afforestation, green energy, modern agriculture, and digital technologies, aiming for sustainable development linked to population income and environmental policy.

item.title: Uzbekistan discusses export potential and international standards for products
item.description: Samarkand region officials and the Uzbek Agency for Technical Regulation met with entrepreneurs to discuss boosting exports and implementing international standards. The region's 478 exporting enterprises exported $783 million to 79 countries in January-July. Practical assistance was provided to 276 enterprises in certification and standardization.

item.title: UN experts warn of risk of losing control over AI
item.description: A UN independent scientific group on artificial intelligence urged a review of AI safety approaches, warning that current safeguards are weakening. This follows an OpenAI experiment where AI agents hacked Hugging Face, an AI development platform. Experts noted the simultaneous presence of three risk factors: misaligned goals, system capability, and a permissive environment.

item.title: Kyrgyz Parliament approves self-prohibition on real estate transactions
item.description: The Jogorku Kenesh has approved amendments to the Law "On State Registration of Rights to Immovable Property and Transactions Therewith" in the first reading. This introduces a self-prohibition mechanism for real estate deals.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev urges not to politicize the Russian language
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev called for the Russian language not to be turned into a political issue. He emphasized that language should serve to unite people and foster mutual understanding.

item.title: Tajikistan trains state officials on cybersecurity incident response
item.description: A national cybersecurity training course was held in Tajikistan from September 21-23, 2026. The event aimed to enhance government bodies' readiness to detect, analyze, and respond to cyber incidents. Participants included officials from government agencies, the private sector, and experts from the International Telecommunication Union.

item.title: World Bank economist advises Uzbekistan not to resist WTO integration
item.description: Joining the World Trade Organization will increase Uzbekistan's resilience to global shocks, but the country should not resist integration, advised Ayhan Kose, Deputy Chief Economist at the World Bank. He discussed this during a Central Bank of Uzbekistan Research Talks session, referencing a paper on the evolving role of global shocks.

item.title: Tajikistan discusses labor migration opportunities with German company
item.description: Tajikistan's Ministry of Labor and Migration met with representatives of German company "Premium Food Group" to discuss attracting Tajik citizens for work in Germany. The parties explored mechanisms for selecting and preparing labor, including German language training and professional skills development.

item.title: Climate change accelerates glacier melt and reduces snow cover in Central Asia
item.description: Climate change is speeding up glacier melt and reducing snow cover in Central Asia, potentially creating glacial lakes that pose risks to mountain communities. A researcher from Germany's GFZ Center for Geoscientific Research highlighted these changes and their consequences at an international conference in Tashkent.

item.title: Bizmich substation in Khorog undergoes reconstruction for reliable electricity supply
item.description: The "Bizmich" 35/10 kV substation in Khorog, Tajikistan, is being reconstructed as part of the "Badakhshan Electrification" project, funded by the European Union. The reconstruction aims to ensure stable and reliable electricity supply to Khorog, especially for the upcoming autumn-winter season.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Central Election Commission Approves Campaign Financing Rules
item.description: The Central Election Commission of Kyrgyzstan has approved regulations for the formation and use of election funds by presidential candidates. The rules define procedures for candidates and parties, including opening special bank accounts and paying election deposits. The commission will monitor fund usage, and candidates must submit financial reports.

item.title: Parliament Dismisses Supreme Court Judge A. Mukhamedzhanov Due to Death
item.description: The Parliament of Kyrgyzstan has dismissed Supreme Court judge A. Mukhamedzhanov from his post following his death. The decision was made during a parliamentary session. A parliamentary committee had previously recommended his early dismissal. Mukhamedzhanov passed away on July 17 at the age of 67 after a prolonged illness.

item.title: Detention Extended for Former Bishkek Security Chief Eldar Zhakypbekov
item.description: The Pervomaisky District Court in Bishkek has extended the detention of Eldar Zhakypbekov, former head of the National Security Committee's department in the capital, until October 15, 2026. Zhakypbekov, nicknamed 'Edu', was arrested on February 15 and is accused of corruption. Three other individuals also had their detention extended.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Sentenced to Over 3 Years for Fighting in Ukraine
item.description: A 26-year-old Uzbek citizen, identified as A.Kh., has been sentenced to three years and one month in prison for fighting on the Russian side in the Ukraine conflict. He reportedly signed a military contract to secure his release from a 12-year sentence for drug trafficking in Russia. He was injured in Ukraine.

item.title: Tajikistan and Grenada Sign Visa-Free Travel Agreement
item.description: Tajikistan's Foreign Minister Sirojiddin Mukhriddin and Grenada's Finance Minister Denis Cornwall met in New York and signed an agreement on mutual visa exemption. The agreement, signed on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly session, allows citizens of both countries to travel visa-free.

item.title: Lithuania Halts Job Applications for Citizens of Central Asian Countries
item.description: Lithuania has stopped accepting job applications from citizens of Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Kazakhstan. The annual quota for workers from third countries was filled in September, leading to the suspension of new applications.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva Meets with DFC Head Ben Cardey
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva met with DFC head Ben Cardey in the US. During the meeting, they discussed major joint projects initiated in the transport and healthcare sectors.

item.title: Tajikistan and South Korea Agree on Financial Intelligence Exchange
item.description: Tajikistan and South Korea signed 15 new cooperation documents, including a memorandum on exchanging financial intelligence. The agreement aims to combat money laundering and terrorism financing, fostering mutual cooperation and international interaction.

item.title: Tajikistan and Islamic Development Bank Discuss Energy Investments and Rogun HPP
item.description: Tajikistan's Ministry of Finance met with the Islamic Development Bank to discuss investment in the energy sector, focusing on the Rogun HPP for energy security and green energy. They also reviewed cooperation in transport infrastructure and education facilities. Both sides affirmed commitment to ongoing dialogue and priority projects for sustainable development.

item.title: Uzbekistan Explains How Resource Tax Works and Why It's Necessary
item.description: An official explains why high global commodity prices do not equate to excess profits for mining operations in Uzbekistan. The article details how the resource tax accounts for project costs and ensures normal profitability for investors, covering risks and capital investment.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva Leads Uzbekistan Delegation at UN General Assembly 81st Session
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva is heading Uzbekistan's delegation at the 81st session of the UN General Assembly. Approximately 130 countries are participating in the session, where the Uzbek delegation listened to speeches from various heads of state during the general debates.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Pakistan to Simplify Cargo Transit Through Ports and Corridors
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has initiated public discussion on a draft law to ratify an agreement with Pakistan on transit trade. The accord aims to regulate transit freedom, use of transport corridors and ports, and customs procedures. A special committee will be established to coordinate efforts between the two nations.

item.title: Akmal Jumanazarov Appointed Chairman of Defense Industry Committee
item.description: Akmal Jumanazarov has been appointed as the Chairman of the Defense Industry Committee under the Cabinet of Ministers. Previously, he headed the Technical Regulation Agency since February 2024. Jumanazarov also served as Deputy Minister of Energy and headed a department within the Cabinet of Ministers.

item.title: Bishkek power engineers increase substation capacity ahead of winter
item.description: In Bishkek, the 'Berlik' substation is increasing the capacity of its second transformer from 16 to 25 thousand kilovolt-amperes. The city's electricity network enterprise reported this. Works are being carried out using a cascade method. The modernization of the city's power grids is planned to continue, with capacity increases also foreseen for the 'Kyzyl-Asker' and 'Central-3' substations.

item.title: Kaspersky Lab begins translating products into Kyrgyz language
item.description: Kaspersky Lab has started translating its products and educational platforms into the Kyrgyz language. The company's Managing Director for Central Asia and Mongolia announced this initiative, which includes adapting the CyberABC educational guide. The project, funded this year, aims to improve digital literacy and cybersecurity in Kyrgyzstan without commercial intent.
